Grave Wounds

Playtest packet: one fight and a week in camp

Version 0.2.2, 7 November 2026, for 3 to 5 people and about 3 hours. One person is the GM.

What this is. Grave Wounds is a d100 game built on real wound records. Where a man is hit comes from the graves and surgeons' returns of his own war. A fight usually ends with men stopping, not dying, and what happens afterwards can kill them just as well. This packet sets four men of a Yorkist retinue at a crossing of the River Aire on 28 March 1461, the day before Towton. They fight once, and then have to get through a week in camp.

What we want to learn. Are the fights tense and quick enough? Do wounds feel fair? Are the camp's decisions interesting, or a chore? Nobody has played this at a table yet, so a blunt "this dragged" is the most useful thing you can tell us.

What you need. Pencils, two ten-sided dice for d100, scissors, and these pages. Everything to play on paper is here, with a hex map of the ford and counters to cut out at the back. If you'd rather, a phone or laptop can run the fight: the wound roller does the arithmetic. Open swares.github.io/grave-wounds/dist/team.html#playtest. It sets up the four men against Clifford's five, and the GM's script can play the enemy. Please tell us which way you played.

The fight

A round is 6 seconds. Every fighter gets one turn, highest initiative first. Each man rolls once at the start: d10 + Agility ÷ 10, rounded down.

The one roll. Roll d100. Equal to or under the number succeeds, and how far under is the margin. A roll at or under a tenth of the number is a critical.

On his turn

  1. Move. Stay, advance up to 4 hexes and still attack, or run up to 12 and not attack. Walking away from an enemy beside you gives him a free attack.
  2. Attack. d100 against Attack, less your penalties. You may first declare an aim at a zone, at a gap in the armour, or both. Each costs 20 of your margin on a hit, and is free on a critical.
  3. Defence. The defender rolls d100 against Defence, less his penalties. Success turns the blow. A critical can't be defended.
  4. Where it lands. d100 on Where it lands, under the attacker's weapon. With a sword, bill or dagger, the attacker chooses cut or thrust before he rolls. A longbow pierces.
  5. How bad. Margin under 20: light. 20 or more: serious. 50 or more, or a critical: critical. A margin of 2 or less only grazes, unless it is a critical: a step less bleeding and pain, and no stop check.
  6. Armour. Armour lowers the severity by steps. See Where it lands.
  7. The wound. Read it from What it does and write it on the sheet.
  8. Stop check. A serious or critical wound marked S needs d100 against the wounded man's Nerve, less his pain and blood penalties, and 10 more for a critical. Players' men add their setting's bonus.
Result He is Which means
Equal or under Fighting on No change
Failed by 1–20 Defend only for 2 rounds No attack; he may move and defend
Failed by 21–40 Stunned for 2 rounds No attack; −50% to his defence
Failed by more than 40 Out of the fight until helped or the fight ends Takes no part: no attack, no defence

End of the round. Everyone bleeds. Then a side with 25% or more of its men down rolls d100 against the best Nerve among those still up: +10 while a leader is up, −20 if he is down, −20 once 50% of the side is down. Over the target, the side breaks: it runs or surrenders.

Lethality. Standard: Blood ×1.5, +20 to Nerve on stop checks, and one fate point, which lowers a wound a step, or rerolls a stop check, recovery or fever roll. Gritty: Blood ×1, no bonus, no fate.

A worked blow

Gilbert shoots at 55% and rolls 31: a margin of 24, serious. The billman dodges at 35% and rolls 72, so it hits. On the longbow column, a 40 is the right chest. His jack would lower the wound a step, but the war bow takes a step off armour, so it stays serious. The thrust table gives bleed 2, pain 2, and S, so he loses 1 Blood a round and makes a stop check: Nerve 50, less 20 for pain.

Wounds

A wound has five parts, and they add up across all of a man's wounds.

Bleeding. Every man has a Blood pool, on his sheet.

Bleed Blood lost What it is
B0 none None
B1 1 a minute Slow: seeping; lose 1 Blood per minute
B2 1 a round Heavy: lose 1 Blood per round; bind within minutes
B3 3 a round Arterial: lose 3 Blood per round; tourniquet or pressure now
Blood left Effect
75% or less Pale and weak: -10% to all actions
50% or less Faint check each minute; -20% to all actions
25% or less Barely conscious: -40% to all actions, can only crawl
None Unconscious and dying

Pain. −10% to attack and defence for each step, counted to 3 steps. Above that, a stop check every round.

Impairments. Each counts once. Attack and defence penalties are capped at −60%.

Impairment What it does Attack Defence
Dazed Stunned: lose next action, then -20% for 1d6 rounds −20% −20%
Vision Vision impaired: -30% to sight-based actions; blinded if both eyes −30% −30%
Breath Winded: no sustained exertion; fatigue doubled −10% −10%
Collapse Collapses; can only crawl or crouch −20% −30%
Stand Falls and cannot stand unaided −20% −30%
Leg Movement halved; -20% to footwork and dodging — −20%
Move Movement halved — −10%
Unconscious Knocked out (check each minute to wake) — —
Speech Cannot speak clearly — —
Arm (weapon arm) That arm -20%; no two-handed use −20% —
Arm (shield arm) That arm -20%; no two-handed use — −10%
Grip (weapon arm) Drops anything held in that hand; cannot grip with it −30% —
Grip (shield arm) Drops anything held in that hand; cannot grip with it — —
Hand useless (weapon arm) That hand useless −30% —
Hand useless (shield arm) That hand useless — —
Arm useless (weapon arm) That arm useless −40% —
Arm useless (shield arm) That arm useless — −10%

The clock. How long the wound takes to kill if left untreated: days, hours, minutes, rounds or instant.

A man with an arm hurt can't use a two-handed weapon: a bow, a bill or a poleaxe. He can only defend until he takes up something else.

First aid. A friend beside him may treat a wound on his turn. Roll d100 against the side's best Leechcraft:

  • Bind: one step less bleeding, 2 steps on a success.
  • Tourniquet: an arm or leg only. The bleeding stops. Left on for hours, the limb is lost.
  • Cauterise: the bleeding stops, at one more step of pain. A success adds no pain.

The camp

After the fight, each day runs the same way. Use the camp log.

  1. Evening council. The four roles decide, in this order. A role with nothing to decide is skipped.
    • Leader: stay, move, and what kind of camp.
    • Scout: where to go, and how the watch is set.
    • Quartermaster: what the men eat, and what they try to find.
    • Leech: who gets the medical stores, and how clean the camp is kept.
  2. The day's weather is on the GM's page, and it can make a night hard.
  3. The night. A man in camp gets back 4 Blood.
  4. Wound fever. On the 3rd to 5th day after the fight, roll once for each wound: 5% for low risk, 15% medium, 30% high. Add 5 with no camp, take off 5 in quarters, and take off a leech's Leechcraft ÷ 10. A septic wound moves a step worse, and is checked every night.

Every 7 days: the recovery check. Each wound rolls d100 against the man's Endurance, plus:

What To the roll
Care: no camp -20
Care: a camp +0
Care: quarters in houses +10
He marched that day -20
He rested +10
A night harder than the shelter (cold, wet) -10
Poor hygiene -10
A leech with the force + his Leechcraft ÷ 10
Battle wounds heal easily +20
Wound fever is hard −25

Succeed by 30 or more: two steps better. Succeed: one step better. Fail: it holds, and at deadly he dies. Fail by 30 or more: one step worse. A wound starts on the track at its severity: light is mending, serious is serious, critical is grave. A wound that would kill in days starts at serious at least, and one that would kill in hours or less at grave.

Step In a fight
Healed —
Mending −10% to attack and defence
Serious −25% to attack and defence, cannot run
Grave −25% to attack and defence, crawls only, defends only
Deadly too ill to fight

Every 7 days: sickness. Each well man rolls d100. At or under the chance, he has the flux. A day or so later, roll d100 for how bad: 1–3 deadly, 4–15 grave, otherwise serious.

CampFlux this week, Endurance 50
Quarters, dead buried or far off0%
Watched camp1.5%
Bivouac12.5%
Quarters, dead unburied nearby4%
Watched camp, dead unburied6.5%
Bivouac, dead unburied17.5%

Food. A man carries 4 days' rations. With none left he goes hungry, so forage, buy or move while you can. Hunting in open country or woods: the Quartermaster rolls Fieldcraft at nightfall. A deer feeds 5 men for a day.

Camps. A bivouac needs nothing, and is poor hygiene. A watched camp needs nothing. Quarters in houses need the quartermaster to roll Persuade, and he must find somewhere that will take them.

The crossing

For the GM.

Where and when. Ferrybridge, on the River Aire, before dawn on 28 March 1461. The Lancastrians broke the bridge, and Warwick's men forced the crossing on the 27th. Before dawn Lord Clifford's men fall on the Yorkist camp there. Lord Fitzwalter is mortally wounded rallying his men. That much is history. Our four men, and the small ford they hold just upstream, are ours.

Read this out. It is dark and bitterly cold. You've been set to watch a ford a bowshot from the broken bridge, in case anyone tries to come round. Then the shouting starts behind you at the bridge, and men with no badges you can see come wading out of the dark.

The enemy. Five of Clifford's men, all regulars. They are on foot here. On the roller they are already set up.

ManWeaponArmourAttackDefenceNerveBlood
BillmanBillJack and sallet50355020
BillmanBillJack and sallet50355020
BillmanBillJack and sallet50355020
BillmanBillJack and sallet50355020
ArcherLongbowJack and sallet50355020

How it runs.

  1. Set-up (10 minutes). Hand out the sheets and pick the setting. Each player places his man south of the water, on the map at the back. Clifford's men start on box 18 of the approach track, 30 hexes away; the GM keeps their numbers on the roster.
  2. Arrows (2 rounds). Gilbert may shoot as they come on and wade, and Clifford's archer shoots back.
  3. The fight (45 to 60 minutes). They close. Keep a note of the time.
  4. The end. The side's nerve check decides it (The fight). A man who surrenders is a prisoner, and the Leader decides what happens to him. If the four lose, the game goes on: Yorkists come up from the bridge at sunrise, Clifford's men fall back north, and anyone left alive is found and carried to camp.

The ford, for this fight. The Aire is too deep to cross except at the ford, the three pale columns in the middle of the river. A man in the ford may advance but not run.

After the fight (10 minutes). Bind what can be bound. Carry the wounded back. Each of the four who can stand rolls d100 on the field:

d100 He finds Worth (Days)
1–35 nothing worth the carrying —
36–60 food, tobacco, a blanket 1–3
61–80 boots, a good coat, a knife 3–8
81–92 a purse or a watch 10–30
93–99 silver, a fine weapon 30–90
100 a windfall: jewels, a paymaster's chest 200–1000

The medieval captain's third goes to the lord. For this test, ignore pay and money otherwise.

The week

For the GM.

The news. Edward's army crosses and marches north. The four are left behind with whoever can't walk. On Palm Sunday, 29 March, snow falls all day, and there's a noise far to the north that the wounded take for the wind. The next day the carts begin to come back. Towton was the bloodiest day anyone can remember, and Pontefract and every village round it are full of hurt men.

The week's weather. Use this table, so nobody rolls for it. It is from the game's weather rules for this place and date, and the snow of the 29th is from the record.

DayWeatherHighLowHard night in the open?
28 MarchHeavy rain43°F30°FYes
29 MarchSnow34°F28°FYes
30 MarchRain52°F39°FYes
31 MarchHeavy rain45°F32°FYes
1 AprilRain52°F37°FYes
2 AprilOvercast50°F36°FNo
3 AprilOvercast52°F37°FNo

The decision that costs something. Where do they wait?

Choice What it means
Stay at the crossing No march. But the dead lie unburied within reach for 14 days, unless the four spend a day burying them.
Move to Pontefract, about 3 miles Each man who can't walk takes 2 men to carry him, so the four may not be able to take everyone. −20 on any recovery check rolled on the march day. Then quarters, if the Quartermaster can find any.
Bury the dead, then stay A day's work for every fit man, and no one forages that day. The sickness chance drops.

Events. Use one on a slow day, or roll d6. Each should make someone decide something.

d6 Event
1 A cart of wounded stops at the camp and asks for food. The Quartermaster must say yes or no.
2 A local man says the well by the camp has a dead horse in it. The Leech may move the water, at a day's work.
3 A stranger comes in with a Lancastrian badge under his coat, begging for a surgeon.
4 A priest offers to bury the dead for what the team found on the field.
5 Forage: the Quartermaster rolls Persuade or Fieldcraft. On a success, 2 days' rations.
6 A rider says Warwick wants every man who can walk at York. The Leader may send someone, or lie.

The end of the week. Make the recovery checks and the sickness rolls, then the feedback. Who is alive, and who can walk?

If you're using the roller only for the fight, that's fine. Keep the week on paper. The travel map can run a camp, but it isn't part of this test.

Quick reference

Cut out or print one for each player.

The round. 6 seconds. Initiative d10 + Agility ÷ 10, rolled once; highest first. Every fighter takes one turn.

The one roll. d100 at or under the number. Margin = number − roll. Critical = at or under a tenth of the number.

On his turn. Move: stay, advance 4 and attack, or run 12 and not attack. Leaving an enemy's side gives him a free attack. Attack: d100 against Attack. Aim at a zone or a gap: 20 off the margin each, free on a critical. Defence: d100 against Defence turns it; not against a critical.

How bad. Margin under 20: light. 20+: serious. 50+ or a critical: critical. Margin 2 or less: a graze (a step less bleed and pain, no stop check), unless a critical.

Where and what. d100 on Where it lands under the weapon; cut or thrust is the attacker's choice before rolling (a longbow pierces). Armour takes steps off: Critical → Serious → Light → Stopped. Part-covered: the attack roll's units digit (0 = 10) at or under the cover's tens met the armour. Read the wound on What it does.

Stop check (S). d100 against Nerve, less pain and blood penalties, 10 more for a critical. Fail: he stops.

Range (longbow). Short to 20 hexes, medium to 60 (−20), long to 125 (−40). Off the map: hexes to the north edge plus the box.

End of the round. Everyone bleeds: at 1, 1 Blood every 10 rounds; at 2, 1 a round; at 3, 3 a round. A side with 25% or more down rolls d100 against its best Nerve still up: +10 with a leader up, −20 if he's down, −20 once 50% are down. Over: the side breaks.

Pain. −10% a step, to 3 steps; above that, a stop check every round. Impairments cap at −60%.

First aid (a friend beside him, his turn, d100 against the side's best Leechcraft). Bind: a step less bleeding, 2 on a success. Tourniquet: arm or leg, bleeding stops. Cauterise: bleeding stops, +1 pain, none on a success.

Lethality. Standard: Blood ×1.5, +20 Nerve on stop checks, 1 fate. Gritty: Blood ×1, no bonus, no fate.

The ford. Too deep elsewhere. In the ford, advance only.
